topics: Acoustics, sound and noise, generation of sound
Puretone and rms values, speed of sound, frequency, wavelength, period, relation between them
Acoustic power and intensity, Inverse square law
Development of Acoustic wave equation, plane wave equation and D-Alembert’s solution, Helmholtz equation(frequency-domain)
Levels, decibel, sound pressure level, sound power level, and sound intensity level
Addition, subtraction, and averaging of decibel
Point source, spherical source, Line source, Monopole, dipole
Array of N sources and continuous line array of sources
Sound transmission: Transmission through two media-Normal and oblique incidence
Transmission and reflection coefficients (pressure, intensity and power), transmission loss
Sound propagation in open or a closed tube
Subjective and objective assessment of sound
Need for noise criteria, regulations and standards
Sound measurement in anechoic and reverberation chambers
Causes of noise and noise control in pumps, compressors, fans, Electric motor, Cooling towers
Mufflers- active and passive-reactive and dissipative
Transmission loss and design procedure for Expansion Chamber Mufflers

partA.description:
2 Questions from each module.
Total of 8 Questions, each carrying 3 marks

partB.description:
Each question carries 9 marks.
Two questions will be given from each module, out of which 1 question should be answered.
Each question can have a maximum of 3 sub divisions.

courseOutcomes.description: To define various acoustic terminologies and understand the physics behind acoustic wave propagation
To analyse the transmission of sound through different media and tubes
To understand the mechanism of hearing, noise regulations and noise measuring devices
To explain various noise reducing measures
